title: Define Incident Classification Tiers
detail: Section 5 mentions that incidents should be classified based on impact but does not provide specific tiers (e.g., P1-P4 or Critical-Low). Without defined levels, escalation to 'senior management as appropriate' is subjective and may lead to delays.
proposed_text: Incidents must be classified into four tiers (Critical, High, Medium, Low) based on the Impact Matrix in Appendix A; Critical and High incidents must be escalated to the CISO and Senior Management within 30 minutes of confirmation.
original_text: Incidents should be classified based on their potential impact to the organisation. Higher impact incidents should be escalated to senior management and the CISO as appropriate.

title: Integrate Specific Threat Intelligence Sources
detail: Section 6.1 mentions threat intelligence feeds generally, but the Risk-Control Matrix specifically mandates the integration of FSISAC and FS-CERT feeds.
proposed_text: Threat intelligence feeds, specifically including FSISAC and FS-CERT feeds integrated into the SIEM.

title: Incorporate Emergency Patching SLAs
detail: Section 6.3 mentions applying security patches during eradication but lacks the specific 72-hour SLA for critical vulnerabilities (CVSS ≥ 9.0) defined in the RCM (CR-007).
proposed_text: Applying security patches to address the vulnerability exploited, ensuring that emergency patching for vulnerabilities with a CVSS score ≥ 9.0 is completed within 72 hours.
original_text: Applying security patches to address the vulnerability exploited

title: Specify Use of Immutable Backups for Recovery
detail: Section 6.4 describes recovery but does not mandate the use of immutable offline backups, which is a critical control (CR-013) for ensuring data integrity during restoration after a ransomware or destructive attack.
proposed_text: Systems should be restored to normal operation using immutable offline backups to ensure the integrity of the restored data, following the BCP/DR restoration procedures.
original_text: Systems should be restored to normal operation only after the threat has been fully eradicated.

title: Include Regulatory Reporting Requirements
detail: Section 7.2 lacks mention of mandatory regulatory reporting, such as the RBI CSF self-assessment or immediate incident reporting to the regulator, which is implied by the Compliance role and the RCM (CR-014).
proposed_text: The Legal and Compliance team will determine if the incident meets the threshold for mandatory reporting to the RBI or other regulators and ensure submission within the required statutory timelines.
original_text: The Legal team will advise if law enforcement involvement is required

title: Reference Recovery Time Objective (RTO)
detail: The term 'RTO' is defined in the document terminology but is never used in the recovery section (6.4) to set performance expectations for the IT Operations team.
proposed_text: Systems should be restored to normal operation in accordance with the defined Recovery Time Objective (RTO) for the specific business service, ensuring the threat has been fully eradicated first.
original_text: Systems should be restored to normal operation only after the threat has been fully eradicated.

title: Document Containment Decision Rationale
detail: Section 6.2 states the Incident Response Manager should decide on containment actions, but it does not require the rationale or the approval to be recorded, which is necessary for post-incident audits.
proposed_text: The Incident Response Manager shall document the chosen containment actions and the rationale for those decisions within the incident tracking system at the time of the decision.
original_text: The Incident Response Manager should decide which containment actions are appropriate based on the specific circumstances of the incident.

title: Add SOP coverage for CC-001
detail: The RCM contains control CC-001, but no matching process step was found in the primary SOP. This is suggested because the SOP should describe the control procedure that auditors will test against the RCM.
proposed_text: Add a procedure step for control CC-001 owned by IT Security. The step should describe Endpoint Detection & Response (EDR) deployed across all managed endpoints with real-time alerting to SOC and identify retained evidence: the relevant control evidence.

The incident response process follows six phases as outlined below. Teams should move through each phase systematically.

| Step | Phase | Key Actions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Detection & Identification | Security alerts received via SIEM, EDR, or user reports. SOC analyst reviews and performs initial triage. |
| 2 | Initial Assessment | Assess the nature and scope of the incident. Determine if it is a genuine security incident or a false positive. |
| 3 | Containment | Take steps to contain the incident and prevent further damage. Actions will depend on the type of incident. |
| 4 | Eradication | Remove the threat from the environment. This may include removing malware, disabling compromised accounts, and patching vulnerabilities. |
| 5 | Recovery | Restore affected systems and services to normal operations. Verify that systems are clean before bringing them back online. |
| 6 | Communication | Notify relevant stakeholders as appropriate. This includes management, affected users, and potentially external parties. |

| SIEM | Security Information and Event Management system used to aggregate and correlate security logs. |
| RTO | Recovery Time Objective — the target duration for restoring operations after an incident. |

This SOP applies to all cybersecurity incidents affecting the bank's information systems, networks, applications, and data. This includes:

All IT systems and infrastructure owned or operated by the bank

Third-party systems that process or store bank data

All employees, contractors, and vendors who have access to bank systems

The following are out of scope for this procedure:

Physical security incidents (refer to the Physical Security policy)

Fraud incidents not involving a cybersecurity component
